name: test-ci

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  automation:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"
      - name: Test repository automation
        run: node --test .github/scripts/close-aged.test.cjs
      - name: Test release version script
        run: python3 -m unittest discover -s .github/scripts -p "test_*.py"

  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@d0cc045d04ccac9d8b7881df0226f9e82c39688e # v6

      - name: Set up Python
        run: uv python install 3.11

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          uv venv --python 3.11
          uv export --frozen --only-group dev --no-emit-project | uv pip install -r -

      - name: License header check
        run: python test/_license/header_check.py

      - name: Ruff format check
        run: uv run --no-sync ruff format --check .

      - name: Ruff lint
        run: uv run --no-sync ruff check .

      - name: Interrogate (docstring coverage)
        run: uv run --no-sync interrogate

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@fa04a1451ff1842e2626ccb99004d0195b455a88 # zizmor: ignore[ref-version-mismatch] master
        with:
          toolchain: stable
          components: rustfmt, clippy

      - name: Cargo fmt
        run: cargo fmt --all -- --check

      - name: Cargo clippy
        run: cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings

  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [lint]
    env:
      EARTH2BUFR_FAIL_ON_SKIP: "1"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@d0cc045d04ccac9d8b7881df0226f9e82c39688e # v6

      - name: Set up Python
        run: uv python install 3.11

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@fa04a1451ff1842e2626ccb99004d0195b455a88 # zizmor: ignore[ref-version-mismatch] master
        with:
          toolchain: stable

      - name: Build and install package
        run: |
          uv venv --python 3.11
          uv export --frozen --no-default-groups --group dev --group test \
            --no-emit-project | uv pip install -r -
          uv run --no-sync maturin develop --release

      # Golden files and real-instrument fixtures are validated only on GitLab.
      - name: Run self-contained tests
        run: >-
          uv run --no-sync pytest --timeout=300 -rs -m "not slow"
          --deselect=test/synthetic/test_wmo_cross_validation.py::test_satpy_adapter_reports_product_reader_limit_for_generic_wmo

      # Keep SatPy/PROJ and the ecCodes binary wheel in separate processes.
      - name: Run SatPy adapter check
        run: >-
          uv run --no-sync pytest --timeout=300 -rs
          test/synthetic/test_wmo_cross_validation.py::test_satpy_adapter_reports_product_reader_limit_for_generic_wmo

  build:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
          - os: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            target: aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
          - os: windows-latest
            target: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
          - os: macos-14
            target: aarch64-apple-darwin
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Build wheel
        uses: PyO3/maturin-action@e83996d129638aa358a18fbd1dfb82f0b0fb5d3b # v1
        with:
          target: ${{ matrix.target }}
          args: --release --out dist
          manylinux: auto

      - name: Upload wheel
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: wheel-${{ matrix.target }}
          path: dist/*.whl
          retention-days: 7
          if-no-files-found: error

  sdist:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Build sdist
        uses: PyO3/maturin-action@e83996d129638aa358a18fbd1dfb82f0b0fb5d3b # v1
        with:
          command: sdist
          args: --out dist

      - name: Upload sdist
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: sdist
          path: dist/*.tar.gz
          retention-days: 7
          if-no-files-found: error

FROM rust:1-bookworm

ARG UV_VERSION=0.9.17

ENV PATH="/root/.local/bin:/root/.cargo/bin:${PATH}"

RUN apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        ca-certificates \
        clang \
        cmake \
        curl \
        git \
        libeccodes-dev \
        libeckit-dev \
        lld \
        llvm \
        ninja-build \
        pkg-config \
        pybind11-dev \
        python3 \
        python3-pip \
        python3-venv \
        unzip \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

    && uv --version | grep "uv ${UV_VERSION}"

RUN rustup component add rustfmt clippy

name: test-zizmor

# Audits GitHub Actions workflows with zizmor. Findings are printed in the job
# log and fail the job (zizmor exits non-zero when it reports findings).

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
      - "pull-request/**"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions: {}

jobs:
  zizmor:
    name: Audit workflows
    if: github.repository == 'NVIDIA/earth2bufr'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Run zizmor
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: pipx run zizmor==1.29.0 --format=plain --no-progress .github/

"""Offline release automation tests."""

import tempfile
import tomllib
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import Mock, patch

import release


class ReleaseTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """Exercise release boundaries without network calls."""

    def test_rc_updates_python_rust_and_lock(self):
        """PEP 440 and Cargo use different RC spellings."""
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            root = Path(directory)
            (root / "src/earth2bufr").mkdir(parents=True)
            (root / "pyproject.toml").write_text('[project]\nname = "earth2bufr"\nversion = "0.1.0"\n')
            (root / "Cargo.toml").write_text('[package]\nname = "earth2bufr"\nversion = "0.1.0"\n')
            (root / "uv.lock").write_text(
                '[[package]]\nname = "earth2bufr"\nversion = "0.1.0"\n[[package]]\nname = "other"\nversion = "0.1.0"\n'
            )
            (root / "src/earth2bufr/__init__.py").write_text('__version__ = "0.1.0"\n')
            branch = release.prepare_rc(root, "0.2.0rc1")
            self.assertEqual(branch, "0.2.0-rc")
            self.assertIn('version = "0.2.0-rc.1"', (root / "Cargo.toml").read_text())
            self.assertEqual(tomllib.loads((root / "pyproject.toml").read_text())["project"]["version"], "0.2.0rc1")
            self.assertEqual(tomllib.loads((root / "uv.lock").read_text())["package"][0]["version"], "0.2.0rc1")
            self.assertIn('__version__ = "0.2.0rc1"', (root / "src/earth2bufr/__init__.py").read_text())
            self.assertIn('name = "other"\nversion = "0.1.0"', (root / "uv.lock").read_text())

    def test_invalid_rc_rejected(self):
        """Reject final versions and branch-name injection."""
        for version in ["0.2.0", "../../bad", "0.2.0rc1;bad"]:
            with self.subTest(version=version), self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                release.prepare_rc(Path("unused"), version)

    def test_rc_push_targets_gitlab_without_token_in_arguments(self):
        """Push only the new RC branch using environment-based authentication."""
        settings = {
            "EARTH2BUFR_RELEASE_TOKEN": "[REDACTED]",
            "EARTH2BUFR_RC_VERSION": "0.2.0rc1",
            "RELEASE_BOT_EMAIL": "bot@example.com",
            "CI_SERVER_URL": "https://gitlab.example.com",
            "CI_PROJECT_PATH": "group/earth2bufr",
        }
        with (
            patch.dict(release.os.environ, settings),
            patch.object(release, "prepare_rc", return_value="0.2.0-rc"),
            patch.object(release.subprocess, "run", return_value=Mock(stdout="")) as run,
        ):
            release.create_rc()
            command = run.call_args.args[0]
            self.assertEqual(
                command,
                ["git", "push", "https://gitlab.example.com/group/earth2bufr.git", "HEAD:refs/heads/0.2.0-rc"],
            )
            self.assertNotIn("secret-token", str(run.call_args_list[0].args))
            self.assertIn("GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0", run.call_args.kwargs["env"])

    def test_existing_rc_branch_is_not_pushed(self):
        """Refuse to update a previously created branch."""
        settings = {
            "EARTH2BUFR_RELEASE_TOKEN": "[REDACTED]",
            "EARTH2BUFR_RC_VERSION": "0.2.0rc1",
            "RELEASE_BOT_EMAIL": "bot@example.com",
            "CI_SERVER_URL": "https://gitlab.example.com",
            "CI_PROJECT_PATH": "group/earth2bufr",
        }
        with (
            patch.dict(release.os.environ, settings),
            patch.object(release, "prepare_rc", return_value="0.2.0-rc"),
            patch.object(release.subprocess, "run", return_value=Mock(stdout="sha refs/heads/0.2.0-rc")) as run,
            self.assertRaises(ValueError),
        ):
            release.create_rc()
        self.assertEqual(run.call_count, 1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

# Installation

## From PyPI (once published)

```bash
pip install earth2bufr
```

## From source

earth2bufr requires a Rust toolchain (1.70+) for building the native extension.

### Prerequisites

- Python 3.11+
- Rust toolchain (install via [rustup](https://rustup.rs/))
- [maturin](https://github.com/PyO3/maturin) build tool

### Development install

```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/earth2bufr.git
cd earth2bufr

# Install with uv (recommended)
uv sync --dev
uv run maturin develop --release

# Or with pip
pip install maturin
maturin develop --release
```

### Build a wheel

```bash
maturin build --release
```

### Verify a signed release artifact

Release wheels and source distributions built by the `build-wheels`
workflow ship with a Sigstore bundle (`<file>.sigstore.json`). Check one with
the [`sigstore`](https://pypi.org/project/sigstore/) CLI, using the exact
workflow identity and the branch it was built from:

```bash
pip install sigstore
sigstore verify identity \
  --bundle earth2bufr-1.0.0-cp311-abi3-manylinux_2_34_x86_64.whl.sigstore.json \
  --cert-identity "https://github.com/NVIDIA/earth2bufr/.github/workflows/build-wheels.yml@refs/heads/1.0.0-rc" \
  --cert-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
  earth2bufr-1.0.0-cp311-abi3-manylinux_2_34_x86_64.whl
```

Wheels built from an `X.Y.Z-rc` branch are published as version `X.Y.Z`.

## Dependencies

### Runtime

- `pyarrow >= 14.0` — Arrow columnar format support

### Optional

- `pandas >= 2.0` — for DataFrame output (opt-in via `as_pandas=True`)

"""Synthetic WMO BUFR cross-validation against reference decoders."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

import pytest

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from pathlib import Path

from . import adapters
from .assertions import assert_nested_rows_match, assert_reference_frames_match
from .builders import (
    BITMAP_MARKER_KEYS,
    bitmap_marker_value,
    build_bitmap_marker_message,
    build_code_flag_combined_operator_message,
    build_code_flag_operator_message,
    build_quality_bitmap_message,
    build_quality_section_message,
    code_flag_combined_operator_case,
    code_flag_operator_case,
    compressed_numeric_case,
    delayed_replication_case,
    edition3_surface_case,
    missing_value_case,
    quality_section_values,
    surface_observation_case,
)

pytestmark = [pytest.mark.unit, pytest.mark.rust]


def _decode_reference(library: str, decoder, *args):
    try:
        return decoder(*args)
    except adapters.ReferenceDecoderUnavailableError as exc:
        raise AssertionError(f"{library} reference decoder unavailable: {exc}") from exc


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "case_factory",
    [surface_observation_case, edition3_surface_case, missing_value_case, compressed_numeric_case],
    ids=lambda factory: factory().name,
)
def test_wmo_flat_cases_match_eccodes_and_pybufrkit(tmp_path: Path, case_factory):
    """Flat WMO fixtures decode to the same DataFrame in all scalar decoders.

    ecCodes is the gold-standard reference for these non-PrepBUFR cases.
    PyBufrKit is included as a second independent decoder because it exposes
    descriptor/value pairs in an easy-to-audit structure.
    """
    case = case_factory()
    path = case.write(tmp_path)
    expected = adapters.expected_frame(case)

    frames = {
        "earth2bufr": adapters.decode_earth2bufr_frame(path, case.fields),
        "eccodes": _decode_reference("ecCodes", adapters.decode_eccodes_frame, path, case.fields),
        "pybufrkit": _decode_reference("PyBufrKit", adapters.decode_pybufrkit_frame, path, case.fields),
    }

    assert_reference_frames_match(case, frames, expected)


def test_wmo_numeric_operators_exempt_code_and_flag_tables(tmp_path: Path):
    """Code/flag operator exemptions match ecCodes and explicit values."""
    case = code_flag_operator_case()
    path = tmp_path / f"{case.name}.bufr"
    path.write_bytes(build_code_flag_operator_message(case))
    expected = adapters.expected_frame(case)

    frames = {
        "earth2bufr": adapters.decode_earth2bufr_frame(path, case.fields),
        "eccodes": _decode_reference("ecCodes", adapters.decode_eccodes_frame, path, case.fields),
    }

    assert_reference_frames_match(case, frames, expected)


def test_wmo_combined_numeric_operator_exempts_code_and_flag_tables(tmp_path: Path):
    """Combined scale/width operator exemptions match ecCodes."""
    case = code_flag_combined_operator_case()
    path = tmp_path / f"{case.name}.bufr"
    path.write_bytes(build_code_flag_combined_operator_message(case))
    expected = adapters.expected_frame(case)

    frames = {
        "earth2bufr": adapters.decode_earth2bufr_frame(path, case.fields),
        "eccodes": _decode_reference("ecCodes", adapters.decode_eccodes_frame, path, case.fields),
    }

    assert_reference_frames_match(case, frames, expected)


def test_wmo_delayed_replication_nested_structure_matches_references(tmp_path: Path):
    """A delayed-replication level list matches ecCodes and PyBufrKit."""
    case = delayed_replication_case()
    path = case.write(tmp_path)
    expected = adapters.delayed_replication_expected_rows(case)

    rows_by_library = {
        "earth2bufr": adapters.decode_earth2bufr_delayed_replication(path),
        "eccodes": _decode_reference("ecCodes", adapters.decode_eccodes_delayed_replication, path),
        "pybufrkit": _decode_reference("PyBufrKit", adapters.decode_pybufrkit_delayed_replication, path),
    }

    for library, rows in rows_by_library.items():
        assert_nested_rows_match(case, library, rows, expected)


def test_wmo_quality_bitmap_operators_match_eccodes(tmp_path: Path):
    """Quality, bitmap and bitmap-reuse operators occupy no bits: values after them match ecCodes."""
    import earth2bufr

    path = tmp_path / "quality_bitmap.bufr"
    path.write_bytes(build_quality_bitmap_message())
    keys = ["year", "airTemperature", "dataPresentIndicator", "#1#airTemperature->percentConfidence", "windSpeed"]
    reference = _decode_reference("ecCodes", adapters.decode_eccodes_keys, path, keys)
    batch = next(iter(earth2bufr.read_bufr(path)))
    values = [(name, column[0].as_py()) for name, column in zip(batch.schema.names, batch.columns, strict=True)]

    assert reference == {
        "year": [2024],
        "airTemperature": [281.5],
        "dataPresentIndicator": [1, 0],
        "#1#airTemperature->percentConfidence": [70],
        "windSpeed": [3.5],
    }
    assert values[:7] == [
        ("B004001", 2024.0),
        ("B012101", 281.5),
        ("B031031", 1.0),
        ("B031031", 0.0),
        ("B033007", 70.0),
        ("B033007", 90.0),
        ("B011002", 3.5),
    ]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("compressed", [False, True], ids=["uncompressed", "compressed"])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("operator", sorted(BITMAP_MARKER_KEYS), ids=lambda operator: f"2-{operator:02d}-255")
def test_wmo_bitmap_marker_operators_match_eccodes(tmp_path: Path, operator: int, compressed: bool):
    """Marker operators with YYY=255 read the element the bitmap points at, as ecCodes does."""
    import earth2bufr

    path = tmp_path / "bitmap_marker.bufr"
    path.write_bytes(build_bitmap_marker_message(operator, compressed=compressed, num_subsets=2, passes=2))
    key = BITMAP_MARKER_KEYS[operator]
    reference = _decode_reference("ecCodes", adapters.decode_eccodes_keys, path, [key])[key]
    expected = [
        [bitmap_marker_value(operator, subset, repeat, marker) for repeat in range(2) for marker in range(2)]
        for subset in range(2)
    ]
    # ecCodes lists uncompressed values subset by subset and compressed values marker by marker.
    if compressed:
        reference_rows = [reference[subset::2] for subset in range(2)]
    else:
        reference_rows = [reference[subset * 4 : (subset + 1) * 4] for subset in range(2)]
    batch = next(iter(earth2bufr.read_bufr(path)))
    suffix = f"_2{operator:02d}255"
    markers = [name for name in batch.schema.names if name.endswith(suffix)]
    rows = [
        [batch.column(index)[subset].as_py() for index, name in enumerate(batch.schema.names) if name in markers]
        for subset in range(2)
    ]

    assert reference_rows == [pytest.approx(row) for row in expected]
    assert markers == [f"B012101{suffix}", f"B011002{suffix}"] * 2
    assert rows == [pytest.approx(row) for row in expected]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("compressed", [False, True], ids=["uncompressed", "compressed"])
def test_wmo_quality_section_with_bitmap_reuse_matches_eccodes(tmp_path: Path, compressed: bool):
    """Confidences, reused-bitmap statistics and a substituted value on a second bitmap match ecCodes,
    in strict mode and in both fixed replication layouts."""
    import pyarrow as pa

    import earth2bufr

    path = tmp_path / "quality_section.bufr"
    path.write_bytes(build_quality_section_message(compressed=compressed))
    expected = [quality_section_values(subset) for subset in range(2)]
    targets = ["#1#airTemperature", "#2#airTemperature", "#2#windSpeed"]
    keys = {
        "percentConfidence": [f"{target}->percentConfidence" for target in targets],
        "firstOrderStatisticalValue": [f"{target}->firstOrderStatisticalValue" for target in targets],
        "substitutedValue": ["#1#year->substitutedValue"],
    }
    reference = _decode_reference(
        "ecCodes", adapters.decode_eccodes_keys, path, [key for group in keys.values() for key in group]
    )
    # ecCodes attaches these values to their elements in the first subset only when uncompressed.
    for subset in range(2 if compressed else 1):
        for name, group in keys.items():
            assert [reference[key][subset] for key in group] == pytest.approx(expected[subset][name]), name

    suffixes = {"firstOrderStatisticalValue": "_224255", "substitutedValue": "_223255"}
    marker_names = {
        "flat": ["B012101_224255", "B012101_224255", "B011002_224255", "B004001_223255"],
        "structural": ["B012101_224255", "B012101_224255", "B011002_224255", "B004001_223255"],
    }
    for layout, names in marker_names.items():
        with earth2bufr.open_bufr(path, strict=True) as source:
            batch = pa.Table.from_batches(list(source.iter_batches(fixed_replication=layout)))
        markers = [name for name in batch.column_names if name.endswith(tuple(suffixes.values()))]
        assert markers == names, layout
        for key, suffix in suffixes.items():
            columns = [batch.column(i) for i, name in enumerate(batch.column_names) if name.endswith(suffix)]
            rows = [[column[subset].as_py() for column in columns] for subset in range(2)]
            assert rows == [pytest.approx(row[key]) for row in expected], (layout, key)
    flat = pa.Table.from_batches(earth2bufr.read_bufr(path, strict=True))
    confidences = [flat.column(i) for i, name in enumerate(flat.column_names) if name == "B033007"]
    assert [[column[subset].as_py() for column in confidences] for subset in range(2)] == [
        row["percentConfidence"] for row in expected
    ]


def test_satpy_adapter_reports_product_reader_limit_for_generic_wmo(tmp_path: Path):
    """SatPy BUFR readers are product-specific, not generic WMO decoders."""
    case = surface_observation_case()
    path = case.write(tmp_path)

    try:
        adapters.decode_satpy_frame(path)
    except adapters.ReferenceDecoderUnavailableError as exc:
        if "not installed" in str(exc):
            raise AssertionError(str(exc)) from exc
        assert "product-specific BUFR reader" in str(exc)
    else:
        pytest.fail("SatPy unexpectedly decoded a generic WMO fixture with a product-specific reader")

name: utils-create-rc

# Manual release cut from main, restricted to maintainers and admins.
#
# main carries an X.Y.Za0 development version. This workflow:
#   1. creates the X.Y.Z-rc branch from main with every version entry set to
#      X.Y.ZrcN (X.Y.Z-rc.N for Cargo), and
#   2. opens a pull request against main that bumps the development version
#      to the next X.Y.Za0.
# Wheels are built from the rc branch with the build-wheels workflow, which
# drops the rc suffix and publishes X.Y.Z.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      rc-number:
        description: Release candidate number (the N in X.Y.ZrcN)
        type: string
        default: "1"
      next-version:
        description: Next development version for main (X.Y.Za0). Defaults to the next minor.
        type: string
        default: ""
      dry-run:
        description: Only print the plan, do not push or open a pull request
        type: boolean
        default: false

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: create-rc
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  create-rc:
    name: Create rc branch and version bump PR
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      RC_NUMBER: ${{ inputs.rc-number }}
      NEXT_VERSION: ${{ inputs.next-version }}
      DRY_RUN: ${{ inputs.dry-run }}
      ACTOR: ${{ github.actor }}
      REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
    steps:
      - name: Require maintain or admin role
        run: |
          role=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/collaborators/$ACTOR/permission" --jq .role_name)
          echo "$ACTOR has role: $role"
          case "$role" in
            admin|maintain) ;;
            *) echo "::error::Only maintainers and admins can cut a release"; exit 1 ;;
          esac

      - name: Require main
        if: github.ref != 'refs/heads/main'
        run: echo "::error::Run this workflow from main"; exit 1

      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: true

      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065 # v5.6.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      - name: Plan release
        id: plan
        run: |
          python .github/scripts/bump_version.py plan --rc-number "$RC_NUMBER" --next-version "$NEXT_VERSION" | tee plan.env
          cat plan.env >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          rm plan.env

      - name: Check branches are free
        env:
          RC_BRANCH: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.rc_branch }}
          BUMP_BRANCH: bump-version-${{ steps.plan.outputs.next_version }}
        run: |
          for branch in "$RC_BRANCH" "$BUMP_BRANCH"; do
            if git ls-remote --exit-code --heads origin "refs/heads/$branch" > /dev/null; then
              echo "::error::Branch $branch already exists"; exit 1
            fi
          done

      - name: Configure git identity
        run: |
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

      - name: Create rc branch
        env:
          RC_BRANCH: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.rc_branch }}
          RC_VERSION: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.rc_version }}
        run: |
          git checkout -b "$RC_BRANCH"
          python .github/scripts/bump_version.py apply "$RC_VERSION"
          git commit --signoff -am "Bump version to $RC_VERSION"
          git show --stat HEAD
          if [ "$DRY_RUN" != "true" ]; then
            git push origin "HEAD:refs/heads/$RC_BRANCH"
          fi

      - name: Open version bump PR for main
        env:
          RC_BRANCH: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.rc_branch }}
          RELEASE: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.release }}
          NEXT: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.next_version }}
        run: |
          git checkout -b "bump-version-$NEXT" origin/main
          python .github/scripts/bump_version.py apply "$NEXT"
          git commit --signoff -am "Bump version to $NEXT"
          git show --stat HEAD
          if [ "$DRY_RUN" != "true" ]; then
            git push origin "HEAD:refs/heads/bump-version-$NEXT"
            gh pr create --base main --head "bump-version-$NEXT" \
              --title "Bump version to $NEXT" \
              --body "Start development of the next release after cutting \`$RC_BRANCH\` ($RELEASE)."
          fi

name: build-wheels

# Manual build of the release artifacts for any branch, restricted to
# maintainers and admins. Each artifact is smoke tested after the build. The
# artifacts that built are then signed keylessly with Sigstore (GitHub OIDC
# identity of this workflow), verified, and stored in the `signed-release`
# workflow artifact (a file and its .sigstore.json bundle for each of up to
# five artifacts). The GitLab `push-wheel` job downloads a run by ID, verifies
# the signatures again, and uploads to Artifactory.
#
# On an X.Y.Z-rc branch the wheels are built as X.Y.Z (the rc suffix dropped).

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      linux-x86_64:
        description: Build Linux x86_64 wheel
        type: boolean
        default: true
      linux-arm64:
        description: Build Linux arm64 wheel
        type: boolean
        default: true
      windows-x86_64:
        description: Build Windows x86_64 wheel
        type: boolean
        default: true
      macos-arm64:
        description: Build macOS arm64 wheel
        type: boolean
        default: true
      sdist:
        description: Build source distribution
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  OIDC_ISSUER: https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
  CERT_IDENTITY: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/.github/workflows/build-wheels.yml@${{ github.ref }}

jobs:
  authorize:
    name: Check maintainer access
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.matrix }}
    steps:
      - name: Require maintain or admin role
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          ACTOR: ${{ github.actor }}
        run: |
          role=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/collaborators/$ACTOR/permission" --jq .role_name)
          echo "$ACTOR has role: $role"
          case "$role" in
            admin|maintain) ;;
            *) echo "::error::Only maintainers and admins can build release artifacts"; exit 1 ;;
          esac

      - name: Select wheel platforms
        id: matrix
        env:
          INPUTS: ${{ toJSON(inputs) }}
        run: |
          all='[
            {"name":"linux-x86_64","os":"ubuntu-latest","target":"x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu","manylinux":"auto"},
            {"name":"linux-arm64","os":"ubuntu-24.04-arm","target":"aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu","manylinux":"auto"},
            {"name":"windows-x86_64","os":"windows-latest","target":"x86_64-pc-windows-msvc","manylinux":"off"},
            {"name":"macos-arm64","os":"macos-14","target":"aarch64-apple-darwin","manylinux":"off"}
          ]'
          matrix=$(jq -c --argjson inputs "$INPUTS" '[.[] | select($inputs[.name] == true)]' <<< "$all")
          echo "Selected: $matrix"
          echo "matrix=$matrix" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  wheel:
    name: Wheel (${{ matrix.name }})
    needs: authorize
    if: needs.authorize.outputs.matrix != '[]'
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.authorize.outputs.matrix) }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065 # v5.6.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      - name: Set release version
        id: version
        shell: bash
        run: echo "version=$(python .github/scripts/release_version.py "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" --apply)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Build wheel
        uses: PyO3/maturin-action@e83996d129638aa358a18fbd1dfb82f0b0fb5d3b # v1
        with:
          target: ${{ matrix.target }}
          args: --release --out dist
          manylinux: ${{ matrix.manylinux }}

      - name: Smoke test wheel
        shell: bash
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
        run: python .github/scripts/smoke_check.py wheel --dist dist --version "$VERSION"

      - name: Upload wheel
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: unsigned-${{ matrix.name }}
          path: dist/*.whl
          retention-days: 1
          if-no-files-found: error

  sdist:
    name: Source distribution
    needs: authorize
    if: inputs.sdist
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set release version
        id: version
        run: echo "version=$(python3 .github/scripts/release_version.py "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" --apply)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Build sdist
        uses: PyO3/maturin-action@e83996d129638aa358a18fbd1dfb82f0b0fb5d3b # v1
        with:
          command: sdist
          args: --out dist

      - name: Smoke test sdist
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
        run: python3 .github/scripts/smoke_check.py sdist --dist dist --version "$VERSION"

      - name: Upload sdist
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: unsigned-sdist
          path: dist/*.tar.gz
          retention-days: 1
          if-no-files-found: error

  sign:
    name: Sign artifacts
    needs: [wheel, sdist]
    # Sign whatever built, even if another platform failed
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && (needs.wheel.result == 'success' || needs.sdist.result == 'success') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - name: Download unsigned artifacts
        uses: actions/download-artifact@d3f86a106a0bac45b974a628896c90dbdf5c8093 # v4
        with:
          pattern: unsigned-*
          path: dist
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: List artifacts
        run: ls -l dist

      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065 # v5.6.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      - name: Install sigstore
        run: python -m pip install "sigstore==4.5.0"

      # Keyless signing with the ambient GitHub OIDC token; writes
      # <file>.sigstore.json next to each artifact
      - name: Sign
        run: sigstore sign dist/*

      # Verify each bundle against this workflow's identity
      - name: Verify signatures
        run: |
          for f in dist/*; do
            case "$f" in *.sigstore.json) continue ;; esac
            sigstore verify identity \
              --cert-identity "$CERT_IDENTITY" \
              --cert-oidc-issuer "$OIDC_ISSUER" \
              "$f"
          done

      - name: Upload signed artifacts
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: signed-release
          path: dist/*
          retention-days: 14
          if-no-files-found: error

name: utils-create-release-draft

# Manual draft GitHub release, restricted to maintainers and admins.
#
# Takes the run ID of a successful `build-wheels` run on an X.Y.Z-rc
# branch, verifies every signature in its `signed-release` artifact against
# that run's workflow identity, and creates a draft release vX.Y.Z (tag
# pinned to the commit that was built) with the wheels, sdist and
# .sigstore.json bundles attached. A maintainer reviews and publishes the draft.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      run-id:
        description: Run ID of the `build-wheels` run to release
        type: string
        required: true
      dry-run:
        description: Only verify and print the plan, do not create the draft
        type: boolean
        default: false

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: create-release-draft
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  draft:
    name: Create draft release
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: write
      actions: read
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      RUN_ID: ${{ inputs.run-id }}
      DRY_RUN: ${{ inputs.dry-run }}
      ACTOR: ${{ github.actor }}
      REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
      OIDC_ISSUER: https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
    steps:
      - name: Require maintain or admin role
        run: |
          role=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/collaborators/$ACTOR/permission" --jq .role_name)
          echo "$ACTOR has role: $role"
          case "$role" in
            admin|maintain) ;;
            *) echo "::error::Only maintainers and admins can create releases"; exit 1 ;;
          esac

      - name: Inspect build run
        id: run
        run: |
          [[ "$RUN_ID" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || { echo "::error::run-id must be numeric"; exit 1; }
          gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID" > run.json
          path=$(jq -r .path run.json)
          conclusion=$(jq -r .conclusion run.json)
          branch=$(jq -r .head_branch run.json)
          sha=$(jq -r .head_sha run.json)
          echo "Run $RUN_ID: $path on $branch ($sha), conclusion: $conclusion"
          [[ "$path" == ".github/workflows/build-wheels.yml" ]] || { echo "::error::Run is not a build-wheels run"; exit 1; }
          # Partial builds still conclude as failure, so only successful runs are released
          [[ "$conclusion" == "success" ]] || { echo "::error::Run did not succeed"; exit 1; }
          if [[ ! "$branch" =~ ^([0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+)-rc$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::Releases are built from X.Y.Z-rc branches, got '$branch'"; exit 1
          fi
          version="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
          if gh release view "v$version" --repo "$REPO" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "::error::Release v$version already exists"; exit 1
          fi
          {
            echo "version=$version"
            echo "branch=$branch"
            echo "sha=$sha"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Download signed artifacts
        uses: actions/download-artifact@d3f86a106a0bac45b974a628896c90dbdf5c8093 # v4
        with:
          name: signed-release
          path: dist
          run-id: ${{ inputs.run-id }}
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}

      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065 # v5.6.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      - name: Install sigstore
        run: python -m pip install "sigstore==4.5.0"

      - name: Verify signatures
        env:
          BRANCH: ${{ steps.run.outputs.branch }}
        run: |
          identity="https://github.com/$REPO/.github/workflows/build-wheels.yml@refs/heads/$BRANCH"
          echo "CERT_IDENTITY=$identity" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          ls -l dist
          count=0
          for f in dist/*; do
            case "$f" in *.sigstore.json) continue ;; esac
            [[ -f "$f.sigstore.json" ]] || { echo "::error::Missing bundle for $f"; exit 1; }
            sigstore verify identity \
              --bundle "$f.sigstore.json" \
              --cert-identity "$identity" \
              --cert-oidc-issuer "$OIDC_ISSUER" \
              "$f"
            count=$((count + 1))
          done
          [[ "$count" -gt 0 ]] || { echo "::error::No artifacts to release"; exit 1; }
          echo "Verified $count artifacts"

      - name: Create draft release
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ steps.run.outputs.version }}
          SHA: ${{ steps.run.outputs.sha }}
        run: |
          cat > notes.md <<NOTES
          Built by [run $RUN_ID](https://github.com/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID) from \`$SHA\`.

          Every file has a Sigstore bundle (\`<file>.sigstore.json\`). Verify a download with:

          \`\`\`bash
          pip install sigstore
          sigstore verify identity \\
            --bundle <file>.sigstore.json \\
            --cert-identity "$CERT_IDENTITY" \\
            --cert-oidc-issuer "$OIDC_ISSUER" \\
            <file>
          \`\`\`

          ---

          NOTES
          echo "Release v$VERSION at $SHA with:"; ls dist
          if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
            echo "Dry run: not creating the release"
            cat notes.md
            exit 0
          fi
          gh release create "v$VERSION" dist/* \
            --repo "$REPO" \
            --draft \
            --target "$SHA" \
            --title "v$VERSION" \
            --notes-file notes.md \
            --generate-notes

# Validation Suite

Earth2bufr validation is intentionally small, real, and readable. The tests
reward consistency with independent decoders, clear fixture structure, and high
impact coverage. They avoid mocks for BUFR decoding: each synthetic case writes
real BUFR bytes, decodes those bytes, and compares normalized tabular output.

## Design Rules

- Prefer one targeted fixture over many broad fixtures.
- Keep each synthetic BUFR message small enough to inspect by eye.
- Compare decoded DataFrames or nested rows, because Earth2bufr's public contract
  is tabular output.
- Use ecCodes as the gold reference for standard non-PrepBUFR WMO BUFR.
- Use PyBufrKit as an independent structural reference when it can decode the
  fixture.
- Use SatPy only for product-specific BUFR reader validation; generic WMO BUFR
  files are documented as outside SatPy's reader model.

## Synthetic Cross-Decoder Tests

`test/synthetic/test_wmo_cross_validation.py` builds standard WMO BUFR messages
from small descriptor lists and Section 4 bit streams. It compares Earth2bufr,
ecCodes, and PyBufrKit after normalizing each result to the same DataFrame
columns. Assertion failures include the fixture descriptor list and expected rows.

| Case | Structure | References | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `wmo_surface_scalars` | Edition 4, uncompressed, two subsets, time/location/weather scalars | ecCodes, PyBufrKit | Baseline WMO scalar decoding and row ordering |
| `wmo_edition3_surface_scalars` | Edition 3, uncompressed, one subset | ecCodes, PyBufrKit | Header and data decoding for the older BUFR edition |
| `wmo_missing_value` | All-bits-set missing numeric value | ecCodes, PyBufrKit | Consistent null handling |
| `wmo_compressed_numeric` | Compressed numeric fields with non-zero increments | ecCodes, PyBufrKit | Compressed reference/increment decoding |
| `wmo_code_flag_operator_exemption` | Active `2-01`/`2-02` spanning code, flag, and numeric fields | ecCodes | Code/flag packing remains unchanged while numeric albedo uses the modified packing |
| `wmo_code_flag_combined_operator_exemption` | Active `2-07` spanning code, flag, and numeric fields | ecCodes | Combined numeric packing changes do not affect code/flag descriptors |
| `wmo_delayed_replication_levels` | Delayed replication of pressure/temperature levels | ecCodes, PyBufrKit | Nested list structure consistency |
| `wmo_quality_bitmap_operators` | `2-22-000` and `2-36-000` bitmap with confidence values, `2-37-000`/`2-37-255` bitmap reuse, then a wind speed | ecCodes | Operators without data bits leave later values aligned |
| `wmo_bitmap_marker_operators` | `2-23-255`, `2-24-255`, `2-25-255` and `2-32-255` markers after a `2-36-000` bitmap, uncompressed and compressed, two subsets, bitmap reused with `2-37-000` | ecCodes | Marker values come from the element the bitmap points at, with its width, scale and reference value |
| `wmo_quality_section_with_bitmap_reuse` | GOES-shaped quality section: `2-22-000`/`2-36-000` confidences, `2-24-000`/`2-37-000` statistics through `2-24-255` inside a fixed replication, then a `2-23-000` bitmap for a `2-23-255` value; uncompressed and compressed | ecCodes | Later bitmaps refer back to the same elements; markers inside a replication decode per repetition in the flat and structural layouts |

The code/flag operator fixtures use ecCodes only; PyBufrKit 0.2.25 compares code/flag units case-sensitively against its bundled tables.

The delayed-replication flattening test is marked `xfail` because it documents
the desired generic DataFrame shape: one flattened row per replicated level. It
should become a normal passing test when generic non-PrepBUFR flattening expands
all replicated levels.

## Synthetic PrepBUFR DX Tests

`test/synthetic/test_prepbufr_dx.py` writes PrepBUFR files with embedded DX
tables (`dataCategory=11`) and checks that `get_metadata` and `read_bufr` see
the local descriptors and sequences, that each DX block's table epoch governs
only the data messages after it, and that legacy IA5 missing placeholders decode
as null. Generic ecCodes/PyBufrKit decoding does not consume NCEP embedded DX
tables, so these compare against values built into the test.

## Earth2bufr-Specific Synthetic Tests

`test/test_synthetic_bufr.py` covers structures that are hard to compare with
generic references without custom external table setup:

| Structure | What is validated |
| --- | --- |
| Local Table B and Table D overrides | User-supplied descriptors and sequences decode to mnemonic columns |
| Strings and code-table-like numerics | CCITT IA5 and small categorical numeric fields decode correctly |
| Missing values | All-bits-set non-class-31 values become null |
| Nested delayed replication | List-of-struct output preserves the readable BUFR tree |
| Compressed constant fields | Compressed references with zero increments repeat across subsets |
| Operator `2-05-YYY` | Inline character data from an operator descriptor becomes a text column |

`test/test_bounded_batches.py` covers `open_bufr` and `iter_batches`:

| Property | What is validated |
| --- | --- |
| Encoding equivalence | Nine template shapes decode alike compressed and uncompressed, flat and structural |
| Table C operators | Operators that change the bit layout fail in both modes; operators without data bits leave later values aligned |
| Batching invariance | Batch size, decode-ahead and byte budget change only where batches split |
| One-shot vs streamed | `read_bufr` equals the streamed batches without provenance columns |
| Projection and list filters | Projected and filtered decodes equal selecting from a full decode |
| Framing and failures | NCEP BYTCNT subsets, truncated-message skipping and strict-mode rejections |

These tests use generated BUFR bytes and local descriptor tables; they do not
mock parser output.

## Running Validation

Use `uv` from the repository root after building the Rust extension:

```bash
uv run maturin develop --release
uv run pytest -q test/synthetic test/test_synthetic_bufr.py
uv run pytest -q -m 'not slow'
```

The test dependency group installs ecCodes, PyBufrKit, and SatPy. No sibling
repository checkout is required.

"""RC branch preparation for GitLab.

Wheel build, Artifactory upload, and KitMaker publishing live in modulus-ci
(.gitlab-ci/earth2bufr).
"""

import argparse
import base64
import os
import re
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path


def required(name):
    """Read a nonempty CI setting."""
    value = os.environ.get(name, "").strip()
    if not value:
        raise ValueError(f"Set {name} in GitLab CI/CD variables or the manual job form")
    return value


def prepare_rc(root, version):
    """Synchronize Python, Rust, and locked project versions for an RC branch."""
    match = re.fullmatch(r"(0|[1-9]\d*)\.(0|[1-9]\d*)\.(0|[1-9]\d*)rc([1-9]\d*)", version)
    if not match:
        raise ValueError("EARTH2BUFR_RC_VERSION must have the form 0.2.0rc1")
    base = ".".join(match.groups()[:3])
    rust_version = f"{base}-rc.{match.group(4)}"
    replacements = {
        "pyproject.toml": (r'(\[project\][\s\S]*?\nversion = ")[^"]+', version),
        "Cargo.toml": (r'(\[package\][\s\S]*?\nversion = ")[^"]+', rust_version),
        "uv.lock": (r'(\[\[package\]\]\nname = "earth2bufr"\nversion = ")[^"]+', version),
        "src/earth2bufr/__init__.py": (r'(__version__ = ")[^"]+', version),
    }
    updated = {}
    for name, (pattern, value) in replacements.items():
        text, count = re.subn(pattern, lambda m, v=value: m.group(1) + v, (root / name).read_text())
        if count != 1:
            raise ValueError(f"Expected one version entry in {name}, found {count}")
        updated[name] = text
    for name, text in updated.items():
        (root / name).write_text(text)
    return f"{base}-rc"


def create_rc():
    """Commit synchronized manifests on a new branch and push to this GitLab project."""
    token = required("EARTH2BUFR_RELEASE_TOKEN")
    version = required("EARTH2BUFR_RC_VERSION")
    email = required("RELEASE_BOT_EMAIL")
    remote = f"{required('CI_SERVER_URL')}/{required('CI_PROJECT_PATH')}.git"
    branch = prepare_rc(Path.cwd(), version)
    auth = base64.b64encode(f"oauth2:{token}".encode()).decode()
    # Supply credentials through the environment, keeping them out of URLs and argv.
    env = {
        **os.environ,
        "GIT_CONFIG_COUNT": "1",
        "GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0": "http.extraHeader",
        "GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0": f"Authorization: Basic {auth}",
    }
    existing = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "ls-remote", "--heads", remote, f"refs/heads/{branch}"],
        env=env,
        check=True,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )
    if existing.stdout.strip():
        raise ValueError(f"RC branch already exists: {branch}")
    subprocess.run(["git", "checkout", "-b", branch], check=True)
    subprocess.run(["git", "add", "pyproject.toml", "Cargo.toml", "uv.lock", "src/earth2bufr/__init__.py"], check=True)
    subprocess.run(
        [
            "git",
            "-c",
            "user.name=Earth2BUFR Release Bot",
            "-c",
            f"user.email={email}",
            "commit",
            "--signoff",
            "-m",
            f"Bump version to {version}",
        ],
        check=True,
    )
    subprocess.run(["git", "push", remote, f"HEAD:refs/heads/{branch}"], env=env, check=True)


def main():
    """Dispatch a release operation from the CI job."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("command", choices=["create-rc"])
    parser.parse_args()
    create_rc()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# earth2bufr

![Maturity: L1 Emerging](https://img.shields.io/badge/Maturity-L1%20Emerging-A4C639?style=flat-square) ![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache%202.0-green?style=flat-square)

Rust-based BUFR (Binary Universal Form for the Representation of meteorological data)
file parser with Python bindings focused entirely on decoding BUFR messages into
in-memory PyArrow tables for ETL and analysis.

Documentation: <https://nvidia.github.io/earth2bufr/>

## Installation

earth2bufr needs Python 3.11+ and a Rust toolchain to build from source.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/earth2bufr.git
cd earth2bufr

# Install with uv (builds the Rust extension)
uv pip install -e .

# Or build the extension in a development environment
uv sync --group dev
uv run maturin develop --release
```

Prebuilt wheels are built by the `build-wheels` workflow and ship with
Sigstore signatures. See the
[installation guide](https://nvidia.github.io/earth2bufr/installation.html)
for how to verify them.

## Quick start

```python
import earth2bufr

# Read a BUFR file into a list of PyArrow RecordBatches
batches = earth2bufr.read_bufr("observations.bufr")

# Keep only some fields
batches = earth2bufr.read_bufr("observations.bufr", projection=["B005001", "B006001"])

# Stream bounded batches
with earth2bufr.open_bufr("observations.bufr") as source:
    for batch in source.iter_batches():
        ...

# Read message headers and table epochs without decoding
info = earth2bufr.get_metadata("observations.bufr")
```

```bash
# Install hooks and run all checks
pre-commit install
pre-commit run --all-files

# Run tests
uv sync --group dev --group test
uv run pytest

# Build the documentation
uv sync --group docs

```

# Earth2bufr Examples

This directory contains examples demonstrating how to use earth2bufr to read
different BUFR file formats.

## Examples

### 01_gdas_prepbufr.py - NOAA GDAS PrepBUFR Files

Demonstrates reading PrepBUFR files from NOAA's Global Data Assimilation System
(GDAS). PrepBUFR is an NCEP extension that embeds local descriptor tables in
the file itself.

```bash
uv run python examples/01_gdas_prepbufr.py
```

**Key functions:**

- `read_bufr()` - Reads the embedded DX-tables and decodes data
- `get_metadata()` - Message headers and table epochs without decoding data

**Data categories in GDAS PrepBUFR:**

| Code | Name   | Description                           |
|------|--------|---------------------------------------|
| 102  | ADPUPA | Upper air (radiosondes, pilot ballon) |
| 104  | AIRCFT | Aircraft reports                      |
| 105  | SATWND | Satellite-derived winds               |
| 107  | VADWND | VAD/NEXRAD radar winds                |
| 109  | ADPSFC | Surface land observations             |
| 110  | SFCSHP | Surface marine/ship observations      |
| 112  | GPSIPW | GPS precipitable water                |

### 02_noaa_nucaps.py - NOAA NUCAPS Atmospheric Soundings

Demonstrates reading NUCAPS (NOAA Unique Combined Atmospheric Processing
System) BUFR files. NUCAPS produces retrieved temperature and moisture profiles
from CrIS and ATMS measurements on the Suomi NPP and NOAA-20/21 satellites.

```bash
uv run python examples/02_noaa_nucaps.py
```

**Key functions:**

- `read_bufr()` - Read standard WMO BUFR files
- `get_metadata()` - Inspect message structure without full decode
- `pyarrow.compute.list_parent_indices` - One row per vertical level, in Arrow

**NUCAPS data characteristics:**

| Property          | Value                                    |
|-------------------|------------------------------------------|
| Vertical levels   | 2211 per sounding                        |
| Format            | WMO BUFR Edition 4, compressed           |
| Satellites        | Suomi NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21             |
| S3 Bucket         | `noaa-nesdis-snpp-pds`                   |

### 03_noaa_jpss_atms.py - NOAA JPSS ATMS Satellite Radiances

Demonstrates reading Advanced Technology Microwave Sounder (ATMS) BUFR files
from NOAA's Joint Polar Satellite System. ATMS is a 22-channel microwave
radiometer used for atmospheric temperature and moisture profiling.

```bash
uv run python examples/03_noaa_jpss_atms.py
```

**Key functions:**

- `read_bufr()` - Read standard WMO BUFR files (ATMS uses compressed BUFR)
- `get_metadata()` - Inspect message structure without full decode
- `pyarrow.compute.list_parent_indices` - One row per channel, in Arrow

**ATMS data characteristics:**

| Property          | Value                              |
|-------------------|------------------------------------|
| Channels          | 22 (50-183 GHz)                    |
| Format            | WMO BUFR Edition 4, compressed     |
| Satellites        | NOAA-20, NOAA-21, Suomi NPP       |
| S3 Bucket         | `noaa-nesdis-n20-pds`              |
| Path              | `ATMS_BUFR/{YYYY}/{MM}/{DD}/*.bufr`|

## Data Sources

### NOAA PrepBUFR

- **AWS S3**: `s3://noaa-reanalyses-pds/observations/reanalysis/conv/prepbufr/`
- **NOMADS**: `https://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/pub/data/nccf/com/obsproc/`

### NOAA Satellite (JPSS / Suomi NPP)

- **ATMS BUFR**: `s3://noaa-nesdis-n20-pds/ATMS_BUFR/{YYYY}/{MM}/{DD}/`
- **NUCAPS BUFR**: `s3://noaa-nesdis-snpp-pds/NUCAPS_C2211_BUFR/{YYYY}/{MM}/{DD}/`

## PrepBUFR and Standard BUFR

`read_bufr` reads both. Embedded DX-tables (`dataCategory=11` messages) are
applied to the data messages that follow them; other descriptors resolve
against the WMO tables:

```python
import earth2bufr

batches = earth2bufr.read_bufr("gdas.prepbufr")
batches = earth2bufr.read_bufr("myfile.bufr")
```

| Feature              | Standard BUFR      | PrepBUFR (NCEP)         |
|----------------------|--------------------|-------------------------|
| Tables               | WMO standard       | Embedded in file (DX)   |
| Local descriptors    | Separate files     | In dataCategory=11 msgs |
| Data categories      | WMO codes (0-6)    | NCEP codes (102-121)    |

TRUTHY = {"1", "true", "yes", "on"}


def _fail_on_skip_enabled(config: Config) -> bool:
    return os.environ.get("EARTH2BUFR_FAIL_ON_SKIP", "").lower() in TRUTHY and not config.getoption("collectonly")


def pytest_configure(config: Config) -> None:
    """Initialize storage for skips that should be fatal in CI."""
    config._earth2bufr_skip_reports = []


@pytest.hookimpl(hookwrapper=True)
def pytest_runtest_makereport(item, call):
    """Collect skipped test reports for the end-of-session CI policy check."""
    outcome = yield
    report = outcome.get_result()
    if _fail_on_skip_enabled(item.config) and report.skipped and not hasattr(report, "wasxfail"):
        item.config._earth2bufr_skip_reports.append(report)


def pytest_sessionfinish(session, exitstatus: int) -> None:
    """Fail CI when any selected test skipped instead of running."""
    if _fail_on_skip_enabled(session.config) and session.config._earth2bufr_skip_reports:
        session.exitstatus = pytest.ExitCode.TESTS_FAILED


def pytest_terminal_summary(terminalreporter: TerminalReporter, exitstatus: int, config: Config) -> None:
    """Print concrete skip locations when CI forbids skips."""
    reports: list[TestReport] = getattr(config, "_earth2bufr_skip_reports", [])
    if not _fail_on_skip_enabled(config) or not reports:
        return

    terminalreporter.write_sep("=", "earth2bufr unexpected skips")
    for report in reports:
        reason = report.longrepr[-1] if isinstance(report.longrepr, tuple) else str(report.longrepr)
        terminalreporter.write_line(f"{report.nodeid}: {reason}")

"""Opening, inspecting and decoding files from many Python threads at once."""

from __future__ import annotations

import threading
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

import pytest
from synthetic.builders import build_flat_wmo_message, build_two_epoch_prepbufr_messages, surface_observation_case

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from pathlib import Path


def _read(path: Path):
    import earth2bufr

    try:
        with earth2bufr.open_bufr(path) as source:
            info = source.info
            batches = list(source.iter_batches())
        return info, earth2bufr.get_metadata(path), batches
    except ValueError as error:
        return str(error)


def _same(left, right) -> bool:
    if isinstance(left, str) or isinstance(right, str):
        return left == right
    return (
        left[0] == right[0]
        and left[1] == right[1]
        and len(left[2]) == len(right[2])
        and all(a.equals(b) for a, b in zip(left[2], right[2], strict=True))
    )


@pytest.mark.rust
@pytest.mark.timeout(300)
def test_concurrent_opens_equal_serial_opens(tmp_path: Path):
    """16 threads opening the same and different files, one of them truncated, while the thread count changes."""
    import earth2bufr

    wmo = build_flat_wmo_message(surface_observation_case())
    files = {
        "prepbufr": build_two_epoch_prepbufr_messages(),
        # Junk between messages spans several open-time reads.
        "spread": wmo + b"\x00" * (9 << 20) + wmo,
        "truncated": wmo[: len(wmo) // 2],
    }
    paths = []
    for name, raw in files.items():
        path = tmp_path / f"{name}.bufr"
        path.write_bytes(raw)
        paths.append(path)
    expected = {path: _read(path) for path in paths}
    assert isinstance(expected[paths[-1]], str)

    threads_before = earth2bufr.get_num_threads()
    stop = threading.Event()

    def change_thread_count() -> None:
        counts = (1, 2, 4)
        index = 0
        while not stop.is_set():
            earth2bufr.set_num_threads(counts[index % len(counts)])
            index += 1

    changer = threading.Thread(target=change_thread_count)
    changer.start()
    try:
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(16) as pool:
            for _ in range(10):
                jobs = [paths[index % len(paths)] for index in range(48)]
                for path, result in zip(jobs, pool.map(_read, jobs), strict=True):
                    assert _same(result, expected[path]), path.name
    finally:
        stop.set()
        changer.join()
        earth2bufr.set_num_threads(threads_before)
